subject: Insurance certificate, endorsements, and scope — Helios Cloud onboarding
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@helioscloud.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@helioscloud.com
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor insurance requirements & COI — next steps

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement is starting vendor onboarding and we need to confirm Redwood's insurance posture before we can move the order form to signature. Attached is our standard insurance checklist for vendors (Helios_Insurance_Reqs_202706.pdf). Key asks: 

- Commercial General Liability: $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate; Redwood to provide CG 20 additional insured endorsement naming "Helios Cloud, Inc." and subsidiaries.
- Professional Liability / E&O: $2,000,000 per claim (claims-made or occurrence — we note preference for occurrence; please confirm).
- Cyber/Privacy Liability: $2,000,000 (claims-made acceptable if retroactive date covers 2019).
- Workers' Compensation: statutory limits.
- Auto Liability (if applicable): $1,000,000 combined single limit.

Additional requirements: primary and non-contributory wording, waiver of subrogation in favor of Helios, and certificate must reference Order Form HLX-2027-0041.

Can you provide a COI and the required endorsements (or confirm if your standard policy already issues the AI endorsements we need)? Our target to get to signed order form is week of July 6 — could you confirm availability of COI/endorsement by July 2?

If easier, our broker (cc'd separately) can pick this up — we can share the exact endorsement language.

Thanks,
Alice Zhang
Senior Procurement Manager
Helios Cloud

Attachment: Helios_Insurance_Reqs_202706.pdf
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Vendor insurance requirements & COI — next steps

Folks — forwarding procurement's requests from Helios. They want COI + AI endorsement naming Helios Cloud and subsidiaries, P&L on limits, and preference for occurrence on E&O (they said preference but expect either). Target: COI by July 2 so we can sign week of July 6.

Aditya — can you confirm if sales agrees to the additional insured scope for CG and whether we can accept their subsidiary naming (Helios Cloud EMEA LLC) if requested?
Laura/Markus — please advise on MSA redlines if we need to make any concessions on wording (primary & non-contributory, waiver of subrogation, AI). I will push external to get broker contact if necessary.

Thanks,
Naomi
Sr. Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Vendor insurance requirements & COI — next steps

Naomi — thanks for the heads up. Quick read: Helios' baseline limits are standard, but we should flag two negotiation points and propose language: 

1) Additional Insured scope — we generally accept AI on Commercial General Liability for liability arising out of our services, but we prefer a limited AI endorsement (CG 20 10 11 equivalent) rather than blanket AI on all operations. Will propose: "Helios Cloud, Inc., and its subsidiaries, but only for liability arising out of Redwood Inference's acts or omissions in performing services under the Order Form HLX-2027-0041."

2) Cyber / E&O: Their preference for occurrence is understandable. Our cyber policy is claims-made. If Helios insists on occurrence we should either: (a) insist on retroactive date to earliest policy inception (we can provide) and confirm extended reporting period; or (b) offer higher limits or an indemnity carve-out. Suggest we try to accept claims-made provided retro date to 2019 and a 1 year extended reporting period — request broker confirmation.

3) Primary & non-contributory and waiver of subrogation — contractually acceptable in many cases, but need to ensure insurers will issue endorsements. Please get broker contact and ask whether the waiver/primary wording can be added without carriers pushing additional premium.

I'll prepare a redline of the MSA insurance clause reflecting the limited AI scope and the claims-made proposal. Attaching my redline.

Best,
Markus Klein
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_MSA_redline_for_helios.docx

Subject: Redwood MSA redline + insurer contact for Helios onboarding

Hi Alice — thanks for the checklist. Attaching our redline to the MSA insurance section for your review (redwood_MSA_redline_for_helios.docx).

Two quick notes from legal: 
- For Additional Insured, we proposed limited AI language (only for liability arising out of Redwood's performance under the order form). Please confirm whether Helios will accept a limited AI endorsement; if not, we'll need to escalate.
- Our cyber policy is claims-made. We can provide a retroactive date to 2019 and offer a 12-month extended reporting period if Helios requires it. Would that be acceptable?

For carrier coordination, please share your broker contact or we can share our insurer contact form (attached Insurer_Contact_Form.xlsx) and our broker can reach out to expedite endorsements/COI.

Attachments: redwood_MSA_redline_for_helios.docx, Insurer_Contact_Form.xlsx

Naomi Feldman

Subject: Re: Redwood MSA redline + insurer contact for Helios onboarding

Naomi / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing the redline.

We reviewed the proposed limited AI language and the claims-made compromise. That approach should work for our legal team provided the COI and endorsements show: 

- CG AI endorsement naming "Helios Cloud, Inc." and "Helios Cloud EMEA LLC" as additional insureds, limited to liability arising out of Redwood's services under HLX-2027-0041.
- Cyber claims-made accepted with retroactive date to 2019 and 12-month ERP.
- Primary & non-contributory and waiver of subrogation language on the COI/endorsements.

Our broker (Laura Stevens at Brookfield Brokers) will coordinate with your insurer to confirm carriers can issue the endorsements without material premium changes. Laura, can you confirm? If so, please provide insurer contact and timeline — we need the COI + endorsements in-hand by EOD Jul 6 to keep the signing schedule.

I’ve attached our COI template (Helios_COI_Template.pdf) for reference and included our procurement contact on the thread.

Thanks,
Alice Zhang
Senior Procurement Manager
Helios Cloud
